answer: Optical physical unclonable functions resist Sybil attacks by binding each agent to a unique optical token. A violet laser illuminates disordered shale particles in resin, scattering chaotic speckle patterns across a silicon mesa photodiode array. An attacker incurs the verifiable hardware cost of fabricating distinct physical tokens and interrogator sensors per identity. However, thermal drift and mechanical degradation alter speckle paths over time, causing false rejections.
